construct: Biallelic NBEAL2 variants impair platelet alpha-granule biogenesis. Platelets are often large, pale or gray on light microscopy, with alpha-granule deficiency and variable thrombocytopenia and bleeding.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding with macrothrombocytopenia, large pale-gray platelets, alpha-granule deficiency, and biallelic NBEAL2 variants identifies gray platelet syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Bernard-Soulier can cause giant platelets and thrombocytopenia but not the defining NBEAL2 alpha-granule biogenesis defect; Hermansky-Pudlak affects dense granules and includes albinism, while Glanzmann and vWD lack gray alpha-granule-deficient platelets.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Electron-microscopic alpha-granule deficiency and the NBEAL2 genotype eliminate the strongest phenotype mimics.
